evidence.quote: | Ok [ "borrow"; m; c ] -> UseCases.borrow ports m c |> render showBorrow

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The blocking rule for borrow, hold and renew is decided in Tier 2 (Accounts.ensureNotBlocked, called from Loans.borrow, Loans.renew and Holds.place). The change removes the CLI's own fines-minus-payments >= 5.00m check, which used to be a second authority. Tier 3 views and the CLI only read Accounts.isBlocked / Accounts.owed or render the Blocked flag. They do not re-derive the rule.

evidence.quote: | Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is added below Tier 4. The change removes the CLI's direct ports.Store.Load/Save calls, its ports.Clock() call and its Loans.renew call, which re-entered Tier 2 from presentation. Renew and standing now go through Tier 3 use cases (commit/query) over the existing ports. The CLI also drops `open Lending.Transition`.

evidence.quote: blocked until it is below {money Policy.blockingBalance}
ensure (not (isBlocked memberId library)) (MemberBlocked(memberId, activity, owed memberId library))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The blocking balance has a single definition, Policy.blockingBalance, and the refusal text references it. ensureNotBlocked reuses isBlocked and owed. The duplicated 5.00m literal and the duplicated owed calculation in the CLI are removed, so this change has one definition for each fact.

evidence.quote: blocked until it is below {money limit}

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The per-type blocking balance and the block decision both sit in Tier 2 (Policy.blockingBalance, Accounts.blockingBalanceOf/isBlocked/ensureNotBlocked). Tier 1 only gains a limit field on the error. Tier 3 renders the limit the error carries and does not compute it.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: Pure changes to the Tier 1 error type, the Tier 2 policy and accounts code, and Tier 3 error rendering. No effect is added and no port is bypassed.

evidence.quote: | Some limit -> owed memberId library >= limit

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The balance values have one definition, Policy.blockingBalance by member type, and every use goes through blockingBalanceOf. However, the change rewrites ensureNotBlocked so that it no longer calls isBlocked and restates the block predicate itself (owes < limit, the negation of owed >= limit), including its own handling of an unknown member. The two copies agree today but are separate definitions of the same status derivation.
